solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like this, stand right?

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
to be is to exist or stand, as in 'let it be'
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone demonstrates a posture and asks whether they are standing correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone not drunk can stand up properly, and the question mark flags that loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has not been drinking keeps steady balance, so standing up straight is a typical test of that state.

clue.text: Exceptional clue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: outstanding, notable, as in a remarkable victory
second meaning: a sign or cue that conveys information

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like praise for a crossword clue; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning striking or remarkable and also a noun for a sign or indication given to someone.

clue.text: All-out effort to eat new pancake

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a blitz is an intensive all-out campaign or effort
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone makes a huge effort to devour a fresh pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: BLITZ swallows N to give BLINTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A blintz is a thin rolled crepe of Jewish cookery, usually filled with cheese, so it is a kind of the stated food.

clue.text: Vote on European split in endless rage

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: in places the European and split pieces inside the shortened rage word
without an end means the final letter is cut off the word for rage

parts.note: to fume is to rage
E is the abbreviation for European
to rend is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A ballot over Europe divides people already furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link-looking word that supplies letters here, the Latin-derived 're' meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct popular ballot on a single question, so it is a type of national vote.

clue.text: Immoral young woman longed to grab uniform

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering society

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the longing word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: ached for means longed for
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A wayward young woman yearned to seize a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Deb is short for debutante, a young upper-class woman formally presented to society.
explanation.definitionFit: Debauched describes someone corrupted by indulgence in sensual pleasures, a near synonym for depraved or dissolute.

clue.text: Play, sure, and go under par on hole

indicators.note: feeling under par means being out of sorts, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
being in a hole or in a tight corner both mean being in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A golfer is told confidently to sink a putt under par at the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under par' and 'hole' sound like golf; the first is the anagram signal and the second means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous Corner is a 1932 stage drama by J. B. Priestley, so it is an example of a theatrical work.

clue.text: Gap etc too old for advertising generally

parts.note: a blank is a gap or empty space
taken as written
overage means beyond the permitted age, too old

explanation.surface: A list complains about gaps and people too old to be used in advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket coverage means publicity or reporting spread across every outlet indiscriminately, rather than targeted at particular audiences.

clue.text: Your duty is to hold tongue

indicators.note: holding something means containing it, so the answer sits inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is their obligation to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold tongue' reads as 'stay silent'; tongue is the definition, meaning a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken mainly in Pakistan and India, and tongue is a common word for a language.

clue.text: Battle-axe has reduced radius, bottom inverted

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word has its final letter removed

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
R is the abbreviation for radius

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry, so the bottom word reads the other way

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point, the bottom

explanation.surface: A battle-axe weapon has had its radius shortened and its bottom flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' looks like a weapon to measure; it is the old word for a fierce woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, which is the informal sense of battle-axe in British and American usage.

clue.text: Rats eating dead fish

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: rats! and drat! are both mild exclamations of annoyance
gone is a euphemism for dead

explanation.surface: Rodents are feeding on a dead fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' is not the animals but the exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a small, often brightly coloured marine fish living on the sea floor, so it is a kind of the stated creature.

clue.text: Dog turned away — smile about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the smile word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word for away runs backwards

parts.note: off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A dog is turned away from the door, and someone smiles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned away' looks like one phrase, but 'turned' is the reversal signal acting on the word for away.
explanation.definitionFit: A griffon is a breed of small wiry-coated dog, such as the Brussels griffon, so it is an example of a canine.

clue.text: Mountainous country with over two rivers — Austria

parts.note: and means together with
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
R is the abbreviation for river, twice
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A travel note on a mountainous land with two rivers beyond it, and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain, so the land is notably hilly and alpine.

clue.text: Bits of craft concerning ornaments

parts.note: to ask after someone is to ask concerning them
as a verb, ornaments means adorns or decks out

explanation.surface: Pieces of handicraft relating to decorations, like Christmas ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests handicraft but means boats; 'ornaments' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterdecks are the rear decks of a ship, so they are parts of a vessel, which is the nautical meaning of craft.

clue.text: Drunk wife I turned on

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word that follows runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken wife whom someone has turned against.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk as a noun means a habitual drinker, and a wino is slang for an alcoholic who drinks cheap wine.

clue.text: A good financial contact?

parts.note: surface reading: a useful acquaintance in banking or investment
setter's reading: a literal touch that is financially rewarding, as in the myth of the king whose touch made gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Contact' looks like a person you know; it means physical touch, and in the Greek myth King Midas turned everything he touched to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a knack for making money from any venture, after the mythical king whose touch turned objects into gold.

clue.text: Kinetic art noticed in school

indicators.note: kinetic means in motion, so the following letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moving artworks were spotted in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinetic art' is a real art movement, which hides that kinetic is the anagram signal and 'school' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, and to indoctrinate is to teach a set of beliefs uncritically.

clue.text: Cut of pork in box, hospital soap in the same place

parts.note: to spar is to box
ER is the American hospital drama series
ib. (ibid.) is the abbreviation for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: Pork packed in a box, with hospital soap kept in the same spot.
explanation.walkthrough: IB is short for ibidem, used in footnotes to mean in the same place.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare rib is a joint of pork taken from the ribs with most of the meat trimmed off, so it is a butcher's portion.

clue.text: Cow just spotted in marshland

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is found inside it, so one word lies within the other

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the Fens of eastern England
just and right both mean fair or correct

explanation.surface: A cow has just been seen in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a verb here, meaning to intimidate, not the animal of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, and frightening is a close synonym for that sense.

clue.text: New plan is source of striking report?

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh plan is the origin of a dramatic news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking report' reads as a sensational news item; here it is a sound made by striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussion is the sound of one thing hitting another, and a report is a loud bang, so the adjective describes noise from blows.

clue.text: Surrender, perhaps as I have, in conflict

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: war is armed conflict
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have surrendered in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the voluntary giving up of a right or claim, which is one kind of yielding; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Watch the end of this item?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
an entry is an item in a list or record

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a timepiece marks the finish of a listed item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but is a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep guard, and a watch is a person or group keeping guard, as on a ship.

clue.text: Jazz genre, a style of Indian music.

parts.note: rag is short for ragtime, an early jazz style
taken as written

explanation.surface: A catalogue entry pairing a jazz genre with an Indian musical style.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework for improvisation in classical music from the subcontinent, so it is a form of that tradition.

clue.text: Soft old wine I consumed for boost

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
O is the abbreviation for old
tent is a deep red Spanish wine
taken as written
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone drank a mellow old wine to give themselves a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is a dark sweet red wine from Spain, now rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To potentiate is to increase the power or effect of something, such as a drug, which matches the verb sense of strengthening.

clue.text: Box of cold sauce

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
sauce and lip both mean cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A container of chilled condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is a blow to the head and 'sauce' is cheek, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip round the ear is a light blow, and to box someone's ears means to strike them on the head.

clue.text: Drug trial arranged at home

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A medication trial is set up for patients in their own homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritalin is the brand name of methylphenidate, a stimulant medicine prescribed for attention deficit disorder.

clue.text: One to give up drinking a very strong drink

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the quitting word swallows the next pieces

parts.note: a means one
to quit is to give up
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone who is giving up alcohol is drinking a powerful spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' looks part of the definition but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian spirit distilled from grain or potatoes and flavoured with caraway, typically around forty percent alcohol.

clue.text: Elba resident, British one, that's kept in isolation

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: kept means held within, so the isolation word is held inside the word for one

parts.note: taken as written
apart means separated, in isolation

explanation.surface: A Briton living on the island of Elba is kept in isolation there.
explanation.walkthrough: B + ONE wrapping APART: B + ON(APART)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was exiled to the Mediterranean island in 1814, so he lived there for about ten months.

clue.text: Tough way to cut grass

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hay is dried grass
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A rugged method of mowing grass.
explanation.walkthrough: RD cuts into HAY: HA(RD)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means robust and able to endure difficult conditions, so it is a close synonym of resilient.
